t: The Administrator shall report to the President and to the Congress the results of the study conducted pursuant to this title, including such recommendations as he may deem appropriate for administrative and legislative action, within one year after the date of enactment of this title.

fable.w: The section only requires a federal official (the Administrator) to report study results and recommendations to the President and Congress, both of which are inside the federal government. The tempting reading is that a formal report with recommendations is a participatory process, but no party outside the federal government is consulted or given a role in any federal decision.
fable.s: The Administrator shall report to the President and to the Congress the results of the study conducted pursuant to this title

qwen_block.w: This section requires the Administrator to submit a report to the President and Congress. Both the President and Congress are part of the federal government. The definition explicitly states that reports to Congress or its committees are inside the federal government and do not constitute participation. There is no mention of consulting with or coordinating with outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision.
qwen_block.s: The Administrator shall report to the President and to the Congress the results of the study conducted pursuant to this title

opus.w: The section only requires the Administrator to report study results and recommendations to the President and Congress, and every one of these actors is inside the federal government. It might look like participation because it is a formal reporting step with recommendations for action, but reports to Congress are an explicit trap: no one outside the government is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue.
opus.s: The Administrator shall report to the President and to the Congress the results of the study conducted pursuant to this title

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Administrator to report study results and recommendations to the President and Congress. Both the President and Congress are part of the federal government. The definition explicitly excludes reports to Congress or federal officials as participation, as these interactions remain within the government. There is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with any outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: The Administrator shall report to the President and to the Congress the results of the study conducted pursuant to this title, including such recommendations as he may deem appropriate for administrative and legislative action, within one year after the date of enactment of this title.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that because the Administrator is making "recommendations," this involves participation. However, the recommendations are directed to the President and Congress, who are inside the federal government. The definition explicitly states that reports to Congress or its committees are "No" because they stay inside the government. There is no mention of consulting with or coordinating with any outside parties (states, tribes, public, experts, etc.) before making the decision or conducting the study.
